cards.name: Blend1
cards.summary: CorelDRAW Blend tool preset. Shipped preview (the .pst file's own embedded thumbnail, not a script render) shows a straight diagonal blend from a cyan-blue square (top left) to a pale butter-yellow square (bottom right), about ten same-size squares evenly spaced and overlapping, colour passing through teal and sage. Applied to your own two objects, it carries the step count, spacing, rotation and colour settings, not the blue and yellow squares.
use_for: stepped 3D-depth or motion-trail shapes behind a logo or headline
colour step ramps between two brand colours
avoid: A plain smooth colour transition on one shape: use a fountain fill, it is lighter in the file and prints cleaner.
Start and end objects with very different node structures: the steps twist mid-blend; match node counts first.
Editing single steps or exporting to apps without live blends: Object > Break Apart the blend group first.
cards.applies_to: two vector objects (shapes, curves or artistic text) selected together: the Blend tool builds the intermediate steps between them as a live Blend group; editing either end object updates it
cards.how_to_apply: Toolbox > Effect Tools > Blend: drag from the start object to the end object (or select a blend), then pick 'Blend1' in the Preset list on the property bar. Script: the harvest records no call that applies a .pst preset (its parameter block is undocumented); the file is C:\Program Files\Corel\CorelDRAW Graphics Suite\25\Draw\Presets\Blend\Blend1.pst. Scripted substitute: StartShape.CreateBlend(EndShape, Steps, ColorBlendType, Mode, Spacing, Angle, Loop, Path, RotateShapes, SpacingAccel, ColorAccel, AccelSize) set to match the preview (approximate; not tested by the harvest).

verified.note: Embedded thumbnail shows about ten evenly spaced, same-size overlapping squares on a straight diagonal from cyan-blue (top left) to pale yellow (bottom right).

cards.name: BOXPANEL
cards.summary: Grayscale brush image shipped in CorelDRAW's Custom Data/Brushes folder (128x128 px BMP). The thumbnail is the file itself (file image, not a script render): a grey 3D box seen from one corner, three bevelled faces in light, mid and dark grey, each with a recessed inner panel, white on black. Pixel-identical to dabble.
use_for: box / package stamp in bitmap painting
avoid: Expecting a CorelDRAW (Draw) preset list entry: no Draw menu or property bar loads this file; import it as a bitmap.
Colour work: it is 8-bit grayscale; tint it (Bitmap > Mode) or use it as a transparency / mask source.
cards.applies_to: bitmap: a loose 8-bit grayscale BMP brush image (white = paint / opaque, black = none, as brush nibs and masks read it), not a live effect on a selected object
cards.how_to_apply: No CorelDRAW menu, docker or property-bar list applies it, and the harvest records only the file: C:\Program Files\Corel\CorelDRAW Graphics Suite\25\Custom Data\Brushes\BOXPANEL.BMP. Use it as a bitmap: File > Import (Ctrl+I), or script ActiveLayer.Import("C:\Program Files\Corel\CorelDRAW Graphics Suite\25\Custom Data\Brushes\BOXPANEL.BMP"), then use it as a stamp, mask or transparency source. In Corel PHOTO-PAINT it can serve as a custom brush-nib image (Brush settings, custom nib; route not tested by the harvest).

verified.note: Grey 3D box seen from a corner with three bevelled faces (white, mid and dark grey), each with a recessed panel, on black; md5 matches dabble.

Large output: it is only 64x64 px and turns blurry or blocky when scaled up; keep it small or redraw as vector.
Colour work: it is 8-bit grayscale; tint it (Bitmap > Mode) or use it as a transparency / mask source.
cards.applies_to: bitmap: a loose 8-bit grayscale BMP brush image (white = paint / opaque, black = none, as brush nibs and masks read it), not a live effect on a selected object
cards.how_to_apply: No CorelDRAW menu, docker or property-bar list applies it, and the harvest records only the file: C:\Program Files\Corel\CorelDRAW Graphics Suite\25\Custom Data\Brushes\RIPPLE.BMP. Use it as a bitmap: File > Import (Ctrl+I), or script ActiveLayer.Import("C:\Program Files\Corel\CorelDRAW Graphics Suite\25\Custom Data\Brushes\RIPPLE.BMP"), then use it as a stamp, mask or transparency source. In Corel PHOTO-PAINT it can serve as a custom brush-nib image (Brush settings, custom nib; route not tested by the harvest).

verified.note: Soft blurred arcs: one bright white crescent with fainter arcs around it, on black (64 px).
